reels.title: The Weed Peel
reels.hook: Close-up of fingers pulling the first edge of weeded vinyl — slow, then accelerating into a fast satisfying peel reveal of a huge #77 race number
reels.script: SHOT 1: Extreme close-up, fingers finding the edge of excess vinyl around a large race number on the cutting mat. Slow pull. SHOT 2: Speed ramps as the weeding gets faster — chunks of negative space lifting away. SHOT 3: Final peel reveals the clean number underneath. Camera pulls back to show the full door-sized number set. SHOT 4: Quick cut to the same number applied on a car door at a race event.
reels.audio_suggestion: Trending satisfying/ASMR sound or lo-fi beat with crisp peel audio layered in
text_overlays: weeding a full door number set
the peel is the best part
reels.cta: End card: your number, your colors — link in bio
reels.production_notes: Film on a clean dark cutting mat for contrast. Use a large number (10"+ tall) in a bright color like fluorescent orange on white or black. Overhead camera angle. Get the real audio of the peel — it sells itself. Speed ramp in editing. Final car shot can be b-roll from any event.

reels.title: Plain Car to Race-Ready
reels.hook: A boring stock Miata sitting in a driveway — text: 'She's not ready yet' — then a jump cut with hands slapping on the first number
reels.script: SHOT 1: Wide shot of a clean but plain daily-driver Miata. Text overlay: 'she's not ready yet.' SHOT 2: Jump cut montage — applying class letter, passenger number, driver number, tech stickers. Each cut is a new element going on. Use speed ramps. SHOT 3: Step back, full reveal of the car now looking race-ready with all numbers and class markings. SHOT 4: Cut to the car on grid or pulling into paddock.
reels.audio_suggestion: Build-up EDM drop or trending transformation sound
reels.cta: Text overlay: 'Get race-ready in 48hrs — custom numbers shipped from Asheville, NC'
reels.production_notes: Best filmed in a garage or driveway with good light. Use a friend's car or your own. Film the actual application process — don't fake it. The jump cuts between each element going on are the content. Final reveal works best with a slight dolly-out or wide angle switch. If possible, get actual event footage of the same car for the closer.

reels.title: Plotter Go Brrr
reels.hook: Top-down shot of the vinyl cutter blade touching down on fresh vinyl — the first cut line appearing
reels.script: SHOT 1: Close-up of the cutter carriage moving into position. The blade drops. SHOT 2: Overhead view as the plotter cuts out race numbers — the blade moving fast, vinyl peeling slightly at the cuts. SHOT 3: Pull the cut sheet off the machine. SHOT 4: Quick flash of the finished numbers weeded and on transfer tape. Text: 'from file to finished in 20 min.'
reels.audio_suggestion: Original audio — the actual sound of the plotter cutting is oddly satisfying. Layer under a trending lo-fi or mechanical beat.
text_overlays: how your race numbers are made
from file to finished in 20 min
reels.cta: Comment your car number and color — I'll mock it up
reels.production_notes: Overhead camera on tripod or phone mount looking straight down at the plotter. Good lighting is critical. Use a bright vinyl color on the plotter for contrast. Record the actual cutting audio — it's genuinely satisfying content. The machine doing its thing IS the content, keep it simple.

reels.title: Door Number Application
reels.hook: Hands positioning a large race number on a car door — the masking tape hinge method visible — then the squeegee starts
reels.script: SHOT 1: Pre-application setup — cleaning the panel with IPA, positioning the number with tape hinge. SHOT 2: Peeling the backing, squeegee application from center out. Show the technique. SHOT 3: Slow peel of the transfer tape — the number stays on the car. SHOT 4: Step back to reveal both doors done, car looking proper.
text_overlays: tape hinge = perfect alignment every time
reels.cta: Save this for your next number install. Link in bio for custom numbers.
reels.production_notes: Film at eye level to the door panel. A friend can drive while you squeegee, or set up a tripod at car-door height. This is part satisfying, part educational — show the hinge method clearly, it's a real tip people need. Clean car in good light. The transfer tape peel is the money shot, get a clean take of it.

reels.title: Transfer Tape Money Shot
reels.hook: Extreme close-up: fingernail catching the edge of transfer tape on a freshly applied number — the slow pull begins
reels.script: SHOT 1: Tight on the edge of transfer tape on a car door. A finger catches the corner. SHOT 2: Slow, steady peel. The camera follows the peel line as the transfer tape lifts and the crisp vinyl number is revealed underneath, perfectly adhered. SHOT 3: Full peel complete. Camera racks focus to show the entire number set on the car. SHOT 4: Quick smash cut to the car on track, same numbers visible.
reels.audio_suggestion: ASMR peel sound boosted — or use a trending 'reveal' sound with the real peel audio underneath
text_overlays: the best part of race prep
reels.production_notes: This is THE hero content piece. Film multiple takes. Best angle is slightly from above, following the peel line as it moves across the door. Bright-colored number on a contrasting car color. Get the real peel audio — crisp and clean. Slow motion at 60fps if your phone supports it. This type of content gets millions of views in the satisfying/ASMR niche.

reels.title: First Autocross Checklist
reels.hook: POV: you just signed up for your first autocross and have no idea what to bring — text over someone looking overwhelmed at a registration table
reels.script: SHOT 1: POV walking up to autocross registration, slightly shaky handheld. Text: 'you signed up for your first autocross. now what?' SHOT 2: Item 1 — Helmet. Show a helmet, text: 'SA2015 or newer. Borrow one if you have to.' SHOT 3: Item 2 — Numbers. Hold up a set of magnetic numbers. Text: 'Your assigned number in your class. Magnetics = no commitment.' SHOT 4: Item 3 — Your car. Quick pan across a totally stock car in the paddock. Text: 'Literally any running car with a seatbelt.' SHOT 5: Cut to the car on course, driver grinning. Text: 'That's it. Show up.'
reels.audio_suggestion: Upbeat indie or punk rock snippet — energy of showing up to your first event
text_overlays: 3 things you need for your first autocross
reels.cta: Magnetic autocross number kits ship in 48hrs — link in bio
reels.production_notes: Film at an actual autocross event if possible. Otherwise, garage/driveway works. The tone is encouraging and low-barrier — autocross gatekeeping is a problem and this content fights it. Keep it fast, upbeat, approachable. The 'literally any car' line with a stock Corolla in frame is the vibe.

reels.title: Why Your Numbers Peel Off
reels.hook: Close-up of a race number half-peeling off a car door at speed — flapping in the wind — text: 'we need to talk about this'
reels.script: SHOT 1: B-roll or recreation of numbers peeling at the edges on a dirty/hot car. Text: 'why your race numbers keep peeling off.' SHOT 2: Reason 1 — dirty surface. Show a finger swipe on a dusty panel. Text: 'You didn't clean the panel. IPA wipe. Every time.' SHOT 3: Reason 2 — wrong material. Hold up cheap craft vinyl vs outdoor cast vinyl. Text: 'Dollar store vinyl isn't it. You need cast or calendered outdoor.' SHOT 4: Reason 3 — no burnish. Show squeegee technique. Text: 'Squeegee it down. Edges especially.' SHOT 5: Show a properly applied number surviving a run. Text: 'do it right, they stay put.'
reels.audio_suggestion: Conversational voiceover with light background music — 'let me save you the embarrassment' energy
text_overlays: why your race numbers keep peeling off
1. dirty surface — IPA wipe every time
do it right, they stay put
reels.cta: We use 7-year outdoor vinyl on everything. Link in bio.
reels.production_notes: This is authority-building content. Demonstrate each mistake visually. For the 'dirty surface' bit, wipe a finger across a panel and show the grime. For 'wrong material,' hold up a thin craft vinyl next to the real stuff and flex them. Voiceover works well here — speak from experience, keep it casual and helpful, not preachy.

reels.title: SCCA Numbers in 30 Seconds
reels.hook: Screen recording or graphic of the SCCA rulebook page on number requirements — text: 'nobody reads this, so I will'
reels.script: SHOT 1: Flash the rulebook page. Text: 'SCCA number requirements in 30 seconds.' SHOT 2: Size — hold a tape measure to a number on a car. Text: '8 inches tall minimum for door numbers.' SHOT 3: Color — show contrasting examples. Text: 'Must contrast with car color. White car = dark numbers.' SHOT 4: Placement — point to correct positions. Text: 'Both doors. Class letter in front of the number.' SHOT 5: Show a compliant car. Text: 'That's it. Don't overthink it.' SHOT 6: Flash product. Text: 'We make them to spec so you don't have to measure.'
reels.audio_suggestion: Quick-cut educational audio or trending 'the more you know' sound
reels.cta: Drop your class and number in the comments — I'll tell you what you need
reels.production_notes: This is pure value content that gets saved and shared. Use real measurements on a real car. Quick cuts keep it moving. The CTA of 'drop your class and number' drives engagement and DMs that convert to orders. Film with a car that has correct numbers as the example.

reels.title: Magnetic vs Permanent
reels.hook: Split screen: one hand slapping a magnetic number on a door, the other hand squeegeeing a permanent one — text: 'which one are you?'
reels.script: SHOT 1: Split screen comparison. Text: 'Magnetic vs permanent race numbers.' SHOT 2: Magnetic pros — hand pulling number off, tossing it in a bag. Text: 'Magnetics: on in seconds. Off after the event. Daily driver friendly.' SHOT 3: Magnetic cons — number sliding on a wet car. Text: 'But they can shift in rain or at speed.' SHOT 4: Permanent pros — number surviving a downpour/mud. Text: 'Permanent: stays put no matter what. Looks cleaner.' SHOT 5: Permanent cons — trying to remove old numbers, residue. Text: 'But you're committed.' SHOT 6: Verdict. Text: 'Daily driver? Magnetics. Dedicated race car? Permanent. We make both.'
reels.audio_suggestion: Trending comparison/debate audio or clean beat
reels.cta: Not sure which? DM me your setup and I'll help you pick.
reels.production_notes: Film side-by-side if possible, or alternate shots. Show the real advantages and disadvantages honestly — the authenticity builds trust. Get a shot of magnetics going on fast (it's impressive) and a shot of a permanent number in heavy rain or after a muddy rally stage. Honesty sells here.

reels.title: Day in the Life: Race Number Maker
reels.hook: Alarm going off at 6AM, hand reaching for phone showing order notifications — text: 'race weekend incoming'
reels.script: SHOT 1: Morning — phone showing order queue, coffee being poured. Text: 'race weekend = busy week.' SHOT 2: Design — screen recording of laying out numbers in the design software, matching colors. SHOT 3: Cut — plotter running, multiple sheets queued up. SHOT 4: Weed — time-lapse of weeding a stack of number sets at the workbench. SHOT 5: Pack — taping transfer tape, rolling numbers into shipping tubes, printing labels. SHOT 6: Ship — handing a stack of tubes to the mail carrier or dropping at USPS. SHOT 7: Payoff — customer photo/video of their numbers on their car at the event. Text: 'this is why.'
reels.audio_suggestion: Lo-fi or indie beat that builds — 'day in the life' trending audio format
text_overlays: day in the life: making race numbers
the best part: seeing them on the car
reels.cta: Every set is custom cut by hand in our Asheville shop. Link in bio.
reels.production_notes: This is small-business storytelling content. Film throughout an actual busy day — don't stage it. The authenticity of a real workshop, real orders, real shipping is the appeal. Show the volume (stacks of orders) but also the care (hand-weeding each set). End with a real customer photo if you have permission. The 'made in Asheville' angle is a differentiator — lean into it.

reels.title: Rally Driver Makes the Decals
reels.hook: GoPro footage of your rally car mid-stage, gravel flying — hard cut to the same person calmly weeding vinyl at a desk — text: 'plot twist'
reels.script: SHOT 1: Raw rally footage — your car on a stage, co-driver calls, gravel, speed. 2-3 seconds of pure action. SHOT 2: Hard cut to you at the workbench, calmly cutting and weeding vinyl. Same person, completely different vibe. Text: 'plot twist: the guy who makes your race numbers is also a rally driver.' SHOT 3: Quick montage alternating between rally clips and workshop clips — same energy, different context. SHOT 4: Shot of your own car with your own numbers/livery on it. Text: 'I make what I use. I use what I make.'
reels.audio_suggestion: Hard-hitting beat drop for the rally footage, then contrast with something chill for the workshop — or one track that works for both
reels.cta: Rally numbers, livery kits, co-driver boards — from someone who actually runs them. Link in bio.
reels.production_notes: This is the credibility play and the single most important piece of content in the campaign. Use your actual rally footage — the rawer the better. The contrast between high-adrenaline driving and calm workshop work is the hook. This tells people you're not just a vinyl shop, you're one of them. Film the workshop stuff casually, not polished. Authenticity over production value.

reels.title: What $25 Gets You
reels.hook: A shipping tube landing on a table — hands reaching to open it — text: '$25 autocross starter kit'
reels.script: SHOT 1: Shipping tube hits the table. Hands open it. SHOT 2: Pull out the rolled number set. Unroll on the table — two door numbers, class letters, all on transfer tape, ready to apply. SHOT 3: Close-up of the vinyl quality — thickness, color accuracy, clean cuts. Text: 'cast outdoor vinyl. Custom colors. Cut to your specs.' SHOT 4: Quick application montage — numbers going on the car in seconds. SHOT 5: Car at an event, numbers looking sharp. Text: 'track ready for less than a tank of gas.'
reels.audio_suggestion: Trending unboxing audio or upbeat lo-fi
text_overlays: track ready for less than a tank of gas
reels.cta: Autocross number kits starting at $25. Link in bio.
reels.production_notes: Unboxing content works. Make the reveal satisfying — the numbers unrolling from the tube is a moment. Show the quality up close. The price point is the hook — grassroots racers are budget-conscious and $25 is an impulse buy. Keep the tone excited but not salesy. This should feel like a friend showing you a good deal, not an ad.

reels.title: Things That Just Make Sense
reels.hook: Text: 'things that just make sense' over a shot of magnetic numbers being slapped onto a daily driver in a parking lot
reels.script: SHOT 1: 'Things that just make sense' text format. SHOT 2: Magnetic numbers going on a daily-driven car in the paddock — takes 10 seconds. SHOT 3: Car does an autocross run. SHOT 4: Numbers come off in the paddock — car looks stock again. SHOT 5: Driving the same car to get groceries on the way home. SHOT 6: Text: 'magnetic race numbers for your daily. just makes sense.'
reels.audio_suggestion: Trending 'things that just make sense' audio or similar format sound
reels.cta: Magnetic number kits — on in seconds, off in seconds. Link in bio.
reels.production_notes: This is relatable content for the huge daily-driver autocross crowd. The comedy is in the contrast — same car, race mode vs. errand mode. Film at an actual event if possible. The magnetic numbers going on and coming off should be fast and effortless — that's the selling point. Keep it light and funny.

reels.title: Tell Me You Race
reels.hook: Text: 'tell me you race without telling me you race' — camera slowly panning across a workshop wall covered in old race numbers, plates, event stickers
reels.script: SHOT 1: Trending audio format. Camera pans across the workshop — rolls of vinyl, number templates, old rally plates, event stickers on the toolbox. SHOT 2: Cut to the garage — spare wheels stacked, helmet on the shelf, tow hooks hanging on pegboard. SHOT 3: Cut to the phone — 47 unread messages in the race team group chat, weather app open for Saturday. SHOT 4: Cut to the car — roll bar visible through the rear window, tow numbers painted on. SHOT 5: Back to the workshop, you're making numbers at midnight. Text: 'the answer is always yes, I race.'
reels.audio_suggestion: Trending 'tell me without telling me' audio
text_overlays: tell me you race without telling me you race
47 unread messages in the group chat
reels.cta: If you get it, you get it. Custom numbers from a fellow racer — link in bio.
reels.production_notes: This is community content — it's about belonging, not selling. Every detail should be something racers recognize and non-racers don't. The 47 group chat messages, checking weather obsessively, the midnight prep — these are universal racer experiences. Film your actual workshop and garage. Don't clean up — the mess is authentic. The comments section will be full of people adding their own 'tell me you race' moments, which drives engagement.

reels.title: Night Before Rush Order
reels.hook: Text: 'Nobody: ... Racers at 11pm the night before an event:' — screenshot of a frantic DM: 'hey can you make numbers by tomorrow morning'
reels.script: SHOT 1: Phone screen showing a message at 11:47pm: 'Hey man, autocross is tomorrow, I just realized I don't have numbers. Any chance??' SHOT 2: Cut to you, clearly about to go to bed, reading the message. Sigh. SHOT 3: Time-lapse of you firing up the plotter, cutting numbers at midnight. SHOT 4: Morning — handing off numbers in the paddock, still warm from the heat press. The guy's car in the background. SHOT 5: His car on course with the numbers. Text: 'we always come through.'
reels.audio_suggestion: Comedic trending audio — the 'here we go again' or 'I guess I'm not sleeping' vibe
text_overlays: racers at 11pm the night before an event:
reels.cta: Don't be that guy — order ahead. But if you are that guy, we got you. Link in bio.
reels.production_notes: This is comedy content rooted in a real scenario every small racing vendor has lived. If you have actual late-night DMs (anonymized), use them — realness wins. The humor is self-deprecating but also shows that you care and deliver. Film the midnight cutting session for real the next time it happens — or recreate it, it'll happen again soon enough. The paddock handoff is the feel-good moment.
